quest.title: Daiya's Three-Day Reverie
quest.description: In a corner of the Veluriyam Mirage, you and Paimon discover a strange announcement speaker, and following the instructions, it seems you can participate in a very unique attraction...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Let us give thanks to fate, dear travelers, for your wanderings have finally brought you here!

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Surely you must be searching for a serendipitous encounter beyond your wildest dreams, an astonishing journey that is beyond your mundane imagination?

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Now, the opportunity for us to fulfill all of our desires has been laid before you, right here, right now!

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Dive into the brand new "Daiya's Three-Day Reverie"! Step onto the grand stage, and you can experience something beyond your wildest dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Swim freely in a pool of Mora... exorcise the phantoms haunting ancient castles... break free from the shackles of gravity...

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Whisper the passphrase: "Take us to the world of reverie" to declare your curiosity and passion, and begin your journey!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that speaker really knows how to work a crowd! Though Paimon didn't understand the details...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Journey? Show? Stage? And something about... A pool of Mora!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! When you put it like that... Paimon's definitely heard of that kind of activity before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, is the person making the announcement Daiya? She must be the director of the play.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if we register, we can become the characters of some of the plays?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It definitely sounds cool! Paimon's especially interested in the pool of Mora...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... that's not it! Paimon just wants to see what kind of mystery attraction is deserving of such a special spot in the Veluriyam Mirage!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's say the passphrase together!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Take us to the world of reverie!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Take us to the world of reverie!

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Really? Just like that?

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: *ahem* Perfect! Your registrations have been confirmed, and Daiya's Three-Day Reverie will begin shortly!

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: "An ancient legend resurfaces, and new clues to a priceless treasure are found. A band of chivalrous pirates hones their weapons and hoists the sails..."

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: "A town floating in the sky encounters an unprecedented crisis, and a miracle-working architect must act quickly to prevent the soaring city from crashing to the ground..."

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: "To save their fallen friends, a lone Hydro Eidolon must break into the haunted fortress, and find a way to lift the curse..."

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: There are three different shows, each with their own theme. Please choose one.

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Find an announcement speaker like this, and follow the instructions to go to the place of reverie!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}! Let's look for an announcement speaker and give it a whirl!

choices.text: Shall we kickstart our acting careers?
Like having guests act onstage in a play.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Wait, how come we didn't notice this secret door before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh! Paimon knows! Let's say the passphrase again, then a new path will open!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Together now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! We did it to register, and times like this are perfect to have a little ceremony!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recite the passphrase together with Paimon: Take us to the world of reverie!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With the clinking of machines, a door opens, revealing a tunnel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knew it! A hidden chamber, filled with secrets!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe! Ready or not, here we come!

talks.objective: Discover the truth behind the curtain

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Why are there so many Water Droplets here... what are they doing gathered around that giant machine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's confused, what's this machine for? And where's Daiya?

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Welcome to the Three-Day Reverie! Surely, you must be confused by the scene unfolding before your eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: Then allow us to demonstrate!

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: C'mon, Loafer, stop napping! Now, Place 1, Action 2!

dialogues.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
dialogues.text: "Let us give thanks to fate, dear travelers, for your wanderings have finally brought you here!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that Water Droplet using the announcement speaker to... play a recording?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It sounds so familiar... where has Paimon heard it before?

choices.text: It's the announcement we first heard regarding this attraction.

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Hustler, you're up! Place 3, Action 7!

response.speaker: Narrator On Speaker
response.text: "The Chief Mate that appears in front of the new recruits is dressed raggedly, covered in bandages from head to toe. It is readily apparent that they barely survived an intense battle not long ago..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers! This is from "The Black Nacre and the All-Devouring Kraken"! This is the part right after we meet the Chief Mate!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The narration we heard then was also played like this... what amazing timing!

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: The Harum-Scarum and Black Nacre are about to reach the pass where the treasure is hidden, hurry up and prep the scenery and props, don't you dare screw this up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That Water Droplet is... operating that device? Paimon can't see how...

choices.text: Monitoring, broadcasting, and operating the mechanisms...

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Correct! The function of this massive device is to control the timing of all the mechanisms in every play!

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Our diligent Hydro Eidolons are constantly monitoring the progress of each show, so that whenever tourists arrive at the designated spots, they hear the proper narration and each prop and device is activated on time...

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: As long as guests follow procedure, a fantastical "Three-Day Reverie" will play out before your eyes!

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Of course, if guests try to leave partway through or behave too unexpectedly, then it'll really impact their enjoyment of the show.

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: We just don't have enough staff to handle things like that right now... Anyway, I think all the guests will behave themselves, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th-That's so amazing! We were having so much fun, we never realized how much was going on behind the scene!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So many props and mechanisms have to be carefully controlled, it must be really hard to pull off these shows...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Is this Daiya talking to us now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you using these Hydro Eidolons to control the "Three-Day Reverie"? Why not just come explain things yourself?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon still has so many questions for you!

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Correct, but there's more to it.

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Everything you have seen, and everything inside this Broadcasting Station, including the Chief Director, Fake Playwright, Loafer, Hustler, and the Harum-Scarum...

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: As well as the other unseen and unheard Hydro Eidolon maintenance staff, of course...

response.speaker: Park Announcement Speaker
response.text: Combine all of these and that is "Daiya"— not a person, but the entire system itself, creator and controller of the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Daiya is not a person... but a system?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a sec. That's overloading Paimon's brain...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows that Water Droplets are smart, but can they actually design such a complicated... system... by themselves?

choices.text: There must be a designer behind the curtain.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Yes, that was the case at first. Your surprise is expected.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Long story short, Daiya's Three-Day Reverie started with the passionate Director Zosimos.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: During his short stay in Veluriyam Mirage, Director Zosimos poured his energy into putting on exciting plays, and never had time for anything else.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: As he spent more time with the Hydro Eidolons, he discovered their intelligence and rich emotions.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Hydro Eidolons enjoyed his plays, and looked forward to the next show. They also wanted to share their enjoyment with visitors.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: An idea grew inside Zosimos's head — Could Hydro Eidolons direct, or even design a show?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So bold! That sounds like... teaching a group of children to be directors!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Indeed, it was difficult. Fortunately, everyone worked together, our joint efforts overcoming all obstacles!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Director Zosimos trained some of the Hydro Eidolons most passionate about plays, teaching them the critical concepts involved.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: After some trial and error, Zosimos wrote several sample plays with detailed explanations regarding the thought behind them.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: With Idyia's help, he built the controller, as well as all the mechanisms connected to it.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: In addition to the lines from the plays themselves, Director Zosimos also recorded lots of commonly used words that we could combine into sentences to communicate with guests.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: After a lot of practice, we finally learned to put on all three sample plays without a hitch.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: The three plays are indeed "The Black Nacre and the All-Devouring Kraken," "Petrifying Gaze," and "Skycastle Saviors"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That is to say... Director Zosimos prepared the foundation and infrastructure for Daiya's Three Day Reverie, as well as left the scripts with accompanying instructions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We definitely never noticed the whole thing was controlled by Water Droplets.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: That's quite the compliment! We appreciate you validating our hard work, and proved many of our ideas correct...

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: This is the reason why we wish to provide you with a token of our gratitude, and show you everything that went into the production of the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We experienced a really special attraction and broadened our horizons! We should be thanking you, Daiya!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Ahaha! Then we continue onwards to our next goal— writing our own scripts!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: To do this, we improve our understanding of "plays" and keep collecting new materials.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: The one called Fake Playwright here collects stories from visitors, and enhances our ideas with those.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Even if it can't meet suitable guests itself, Fake Playwright talks to other Hydro Eidolons about their encounters.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So when we tell our stories to Fake Playwright, it helps you write new plays!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Exactly! If you have time, please talk with Fake Playwright more!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Also, please continue to enjoy your time in Veluriyam Mirage, and please talk more with the other Hydro Eidolons here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No worries! Paimon and {NICKNAME} love it here, we'll definitely provide you with lots of great material!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Actually, there's something else... Paimon's been curious about it for a while!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why is it called "Three-Day Reverie"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could it be that... Director Zosimos spent three days on each play? Or maybe, like, three days in total?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Yesterday," "today," and "tomorrow"? Sounds reasonable to Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means Director Zosimos... I mean, all of Daiya, is working so very hard on the plays, day after day!

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Nice one! Unfortunately, it's not quite that deep.

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: Actually, the true meaning behind "three days" is...

response.speaker: Daiya
response.text: "Eh, plenty of time left to do it tomorrow," "Maybe I'll really be in the zone tomorrow," and "If I don't finish it tomorrow I'm dead meat".

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously!?

choices.text: And someone to look over the scripts, right?
